text_fidelity_a:
Sennheiser HD 598 SR Open-Back Headphone "Discontinued by manufacturer" My household has a variety of headphone fans in it. The headphone level of appreciation varies from "I will listen to anything as long as it works" to "I don't hear that sound exactly as I want to, so these are no good". I am in the middle. I love a good headphone, but I am not addicted to analyze every single sound and micro focus on them. What I am looking for is a headphone which has good sound separation, realistic presentation, but not too much distortion or muffled sound.

My purpose for wanting headphones with a cord was duo-fold. I want a set of headphones to listen to my desktop or laptop in my living room while people are watching TV, and I also wanted a set of headphones for my tablet so I could watch video demonstrations for my spinning wheel, knitting, and other crafts in the living room while the rest of the family is watching TV and I need to a quick refresher on a project I am working on.

WHAT ARE THESE HEADPHONES LIKE?
In the box (a nice box with excellent protection for the headphones), there is a set of headphones, two cords, and an extra plug adapter. The headphones themselves are lightweight for what they are. They are marked R and L so that you will put them on the correctly way easily. The ear cushions are a velveteen fabric which a lightweight foam inside. The cord jack is on the left ear phone. The top of the headphones has a soft leatherette foam which is very soft and easily squished.

The long cord measures about 118 inches. It comes with a large jack for stereos on one end and the smaller jack which fits into the headphones. The additional adapter for the smaller jack which fits into phones and tablets. The smaller cord measures approximately 48 inches and has a phone answering. This one has a smaller jack for phones and tablets.

HOW DO THESE HEADPHONES FIT?
I found that these headphones fit everyone in the family very nicely. Even my headphone fanatic liked them although he said his phones were a little nicer but not much.

HOW DO THESE HEADPHONES PERFORM?
I really like these. I have tried them with music, videos, movies, and other sounds from classes to classical. I find them to be realistic and high quality. It feels like I am in the room with the sounds - hearing squeaking of chairs, or fingers on strings - but yet it feels more natural than sound proof headphones. I can still hear what is going on around me, so if really loud music is happening in the room, these are not overly helpful, but that does not happen here so I am fine with them.

I found the sound clarity to be nice. No muffled sounds or blurry sound with these that I have noticed thus far. The bass is nice- not too much, but not overwhelming either. Of course, that depends on the recording I am listening to. There are no controls on the headphones.

Due to the cushioning these are comfortable. If I have a tender head (such as headache type day) they tend to hit a sensitive area of my head so I can not wear them as long as I would like, but most of the time, I can wear them comfortably for extended periods of time. It is nice because I can hear what is going on in the room around me if I need to so it does not block me from having to pay attention to things around me when necessary.

HOW DO THESE WORK WITH A TABLET?
I found these to work very well with my tablet. Using them for visual lessons at my spinning wheel and knitting chair is perfect- just what I wanted. I can hear what I need and not feel closed in with them on either.

CAN OTHER PEOPLE HEAR THEM IN A QUIET ROOM?
That is the one drawback about these headphones- if you are in a library, or quiet room, people around you will be able to hear what you are listening to unless it is very low volume and then you will have to strain to hear.

HOW DO THEY WORK WITH A PHONE?
I have not used them with my phone yet so have not had the chance to use the phone features. I tend to use my tablet most of the time. I will update when I have experience in that area to add.

OTHER COMMENTS
My son who is the headphone fanatic was even impressed with these headphones. He has several top line headphones (including Turtle Beach) and said that he was very impressed by the definition of sound, balanced bass and treble and clarity of these headphones. From him that is a compliment. He is rather stingy with glowing comments on most things electronic.

THE BOTTOM LINE
For the price of these headphones, this is a really nice set. Sound is clear, balanced, and realistic. The headphones are comfortable and well cushioned, making them wearable for extended periods of time. Lots of great sound and detail, yet the ability to hear the room around make them practical for use in a multitasking situation. They work great with tablets, laptops, and desktop although I have not tested a lot with my phone yet, my son has and they work great.

RATING
FIVE stars for these headphones. I am very happy with them. I plan to test in the future for gaming and phone answering and will update at that time.
text_fidelity_b: Sennheiser HD 598 SR Open-Back Headphone "Discontinued by manufacturer"

LENRUE Portable Wireless Bluetooth Speaker with Built-in-Mic,Handsfree Call,AUX Line,TF Card for iPhone Ipad Android Smartphone and More (Grey) I've been wanting my own bluetooth speaker forever. The interesting thing is that I'm not even interested in the bluetooth capability. I want the aux connection for my first generation iPod, which doesn't have bluetooth technology. My iPhone just doesn't have the space for all the music I have on the iPod, plus I don't want to use up data streaming Pandora. Additionally, bluetooth and getting stuff to connect is just a pain. So, I've never tried to connect via bluetooth only the aux.

At first I thought I had dud. I charged it and went to push the power button and nothing happened. I read the tiny print in the instructions and still nothing. So, I went on YouTube to see if anyone made video about using this and of course there is! So, you have to press the power button until the device glows blue and beeps! No where on the instructions does it say to do this! So, once you do this, then you can follow the directions to use the speaker. If you are going to just use the aux plug then push the "M" button, which I think stands for mode. You're good to go.

Now this is tiny, so you're going to get a lot of output, but it what it does put out is a decent sound. I have used mine in a small pavilion for a party and on my front porch. At the party depending on the song, a few downloaded from the early aughts were too quiet to hear, but songs downloaded from iTunes or from CDs came out loud enough to hear throughout the pavilion. Just make sure the volume is up on your speaker AND your device. I've used for about 12 hours total. 4 hours here, 4 hours there, etc., and I still haven't charged it. So it holds a good charge to last through a party or an afternoon lounging on the porch.

You get an aux cord and a USB charging cord. So you can charge it on the computer or with a charger plug that uses a USB plug. The light ring turns red when charging and goes off when it's fully charged. The ring glows blue when it is on. It flashes when it it searching or looking for a bluetooth device. I bought this after a family member refused to let me use his "expensive someone is going to steal it" bluetooth speaker even though he never uses it (and I'm never in a situation to have someone steal it.)
text_fidelity_b: LENRUE Portable Wireless Bluetooth Speaker with Built-in-Mic,Handsfree Call,AUX Line,TF Card for iPhone Ipad Android Smartphone and More (Grey)

text_fidelity_a:
Cisco-Linksys E4200 Dual-Band Wireless-N Router,Black I bought the Cisco E4200 and the Asus RT-N56U. The RT-N56U was better than the E4200 in strength and speed. Transferring files from laptop to NAS server was much faster with the ASUS both wired and wireless. I however decided to stay with the Cisco because the attached USB hard drive (NTFS) works flawlessly with Windows Backup (not the case with the RT-N56U).

Anyhow, I just switched to AT&T U-verse and tried to have the E4200 get an internet IP address automatically. For some reason it didn't. The ASUS here performed great, as soon as I plugged the cable from AT&T modem/router it configured itself. Amazing! Again... I need those backups in NTFS drives, otherwise I would stick with the RT-N56U.

After trying to troubleshoot myself and losing connection with their chat support, I had to call tech support (in India or surrounding areas). I spent almost hour and a half on the phone, resetting and rebooting everything. The router would just not get an internet IP address. They suggested that the router may be defective, but that I should call AT&T and see if there was something they could do on their end???

Instead of doing that, I drove to my sister house and got her E4200(I did the same setup in her house the week before and it worked well). When I plugged it in, it got the internet IP address immediately, no problems at all.

Both routers had the exact same firmware and settings which indicated to me that the problem was most likely with my E4200.

Again to call Cisco tech support. I explained what happened and told the tech that I had disconnected the router, and that I wanted a replacement. After many questions about how many PCs and laptops I had in my house -irrelevant to the case-, he asked me if there was a cable in lan port one, I replied NO, then he asked the same question about port 2, I replied NO, and so on, until he asked me if there was power going to the router, to which I obviously reply NO. So he said sarcastically 'how do you expect the router to work if it is disconnected?'. I replied 'what part of "I disconnected the router" you did not understand. Misunderstandings like this happened with all the technicians I spoke to.

Another one told me that I had voided my warranty for upgrading the firmware in the router. She scolded me for doing so stating that 3rd party firmware can have bricked the router. I explained to her that I downloaded the firmware from the Cisco support website. She kept going on. I am still trying to figure out where she got the idea that I got 3rd party firmware. What a show of ignorance!

When I asked for a supervisor, they put me on hold for 28 min. After that I was told that there was nobody available. Then the call got mysteriously disconnected when I asked the tech for his full name and badge number.

It is not only Cisco, I know. Many companies do it this way. But it is upsetting that Cisco can not source people who understand and speak English well enough to have a professional conversation. Based on this experience I wonder if these Cisco 'technicians' hold at least a high school diploma.
Yeah, they offer support 24-7-365, but it is not real support if they can not help you or even understand you.

My final advice, if you go for it, test the every single feature of the router. If you find any flaw, deal with Amazon, exchange it or get a refund. Do not try to deal with Cisco-Linksys. It is not worth the aggravation.
text_fidelity_b: Cisco-Linksys E4200 Dual-Band Wireless-N Router,Black

Konnek Stein True Wireless Earbuds, Bluetooth 5.1 Active Noise Cancelling Headphones, Sliding Design Charging Case 500mAh, IPX4 Waterproof, Deep Bass Built-in Mic Call for Business & Sports - Black The KONNEK STEIN True Wireless Earbuds are a decent set of wireless earbuds. The sound quality is good, I’ve been using them with music and streaming shows, and I haven’t been disappointed with the sound quality.

I’m not as pleased with the short battery life, touch controls, and lack of audio cues.

I get about 2-3 hours of playback per charge. It’s rare for me to battery drain earbuds, but with this pair, I hear the low battery chime every time I use them.

The touch controls and lack of audio cues go together. The touch controls are super easy to activate on accident. More than once I’ve taken the earbuds out only to find I hit Play while doing so, and they kept playing music. I also activate random controls when adjusting the earbuds in my ears … and I don’t always know what I’ve done. Did I turn ANC on or off? The audio cues are just beeps, not an announcement like “ANC on/ANC off.”

I like the design of the case. It has a sliding top, so you can actually clean the entire area where the earbuds sit. When you put the earbuds inside the case, a light flashes to show their battery level. The case charges wirelessly or via USB-C. There’s only one LED light on the outside of the case, it’s easy to miss when you’re trying to see if the case is charging or not.
text_fidelity_b: Konnek Stein True Wireless Earbuds, Bluetooth 5.1 Active Noise Cancelling Headphones, Sliding Design Charging Case 500mAh, IPX4 Waterproof, Deep Bass Built-in Mic Call for Business & Sports - Black

Asus support informs me that I should buy a third party DVD playing app as Microsoft won't let them include it. Really. I ended up researching and finding VLC player but come on. Finally, I'm very used to having the function keys be utility keys. Brightness, volume, etc. And I like it that way. I don't use the F functions often (F11 is about the only one) and prefer to use the fn key for them when I do. Asus is set up to do the opposite. Most other manufacturers give you a way to reverse that behavior. EIther a fn lock key or a bios setting or something. Not Asus. Nope, you're stuck with it the way they like it.

Unfortunately I'm stuck with this laptop since Amazon has a lousy return policy on computers. Maybe some 13 year old will think it's cool and want to buy it. I hope so.

text_fidelity_a:

We have two 55" televisions and the one in our master bedroom has the Denon sound base under it and that unit has simply been outstanding. I was actually looking to just buy a second Denon for the living room tv and chose this Bose unit due to the one time sale and the Bose reputation.

This unit sits directly under our 55" Vizio smart tv and connects with the digital audio optical cable - just like the Denon base. I turned off the tv's physical speakers and let the Bose take over. The sound is full and significantly improved over the thin tv speakers. The unit shines when watching movies that have lots of rich soundtrack music and when you use the Dialogue button to soften background sounds and highlight conversation type dialogue.

The Bluetooth connected with my LG V10 phone and my fourth generation Fiire tablet immediately, allowing me to play music and my audio book through the Bose. Very nice extra functionality - the Denon does this as well. The Bose includes a universal remote control that requires some effort to set up correctly and completely. However! Once the cursing and hair pulling was over, I got it done. The Bose remote now operates our television, the Bose base, and our TiVo/cable box exactly as the cable remote does.

My one star deduction is because the only way to use the Bose Solo is with their included remote control. There are no physical buttons on the machine and that strikes me as a real design flaw. If you break or lose this proprietary remote you cannot even turn the Bose on or off, much less actually use it for sound. At least the Denon sound base can be operated manually or trained to respond to other remote controls with three steps. For me this Bose Solo is worth the price I paid (under three hundred bucks) and it is equal to the Denon in sound quality. But for overall value and ease of use, the Denon is the five star product.
text_fidelity_b: Bose Solo 15 Series II TV Sound System

text_fidelity_a:
Garmin nüvi 42LM 4.3-Inch Portable Vehicle GPS with Lifetime Maps (US) (Discontinued by Manufacturer) I bought this trusting the good reviews. I live in an area undergoing major road construction on all the highways, and I wanted the GPS to help me route around it when I run errands and go to appointments. I figured the "lifetime map updates" feature would ensure this GPS shows the latest road closures to get me through the city without trouble. WRONG.

Not only does it NOT show the ongoing road construction they started months ago near my house, but it has tried to send me off an exit on another highway that has been closed for 2+ years! And when I couldn't take that exit, it refused to reroute, and kept trying to get me to take the next exit to turn around and then sent me BACK to the long-closed exit. Almost NONE of the road closures are on the GPS map, and it will not reroute even when I hit the reroute button. It is very frustrating.

We have taken the latest map updates, and even contacted Garmin, whose response was that they were sorry they had a backlog of "a lot of updates" and they were "trying to put them in as quickly as possible" -- but sending me to an exit that's been closed over 2 years says otherwise. I HATE this GPS. I only gave it 2 stars because I like the graphics options and it lets you take screen shots of the map. If it WORKED properly, I'd say it could have been a great GPS, but it doesn't do what it promised.
text_fidelity_b: Garmin nüvi 42LM 4.3-Inch Portable Vehicle GPS with Lifetime Maps (US) (Discontinued by Manufacturer)

Kindle Paperwhite 3G, 6" High Resolution Display with Built-in Light, Free 3G + Wi-Fi - Includes Special Offers [Previous Generation - 5th] I have always loved the Keyboard version (and still do), but unfortunately without the benefit of backlighting and the poor selection of cases with adequate lighting (I've ordered and returned several), I started to use it less and less - and used my Iphone App almost exclusively. But I really wanted to use a Kindle which was designed primarily for reading books as opposed to the small screen of a Smart phone. And I'm not about to go lugging around an Ipad day after day.

Last year I purchased a Kindle Touch but was extremely unhappy with the instability of the touch screen and other issues with that model. So I bought the aforementioned Keyboard and made do with it. I should add that I have owned five Kindles since their launch in 2007. When the Paperwhite was announced, I immediately got one for my husband while I waited for a 3g model for myself.

Initially I was a little disappointed with the Paperwhite because of my own lack of patience and constant comparing it to my other devices. I had to get use to swiping the screen to wake it up, understand the basic settings operations, and generally become comfortable with this model. I have to admit that I had contacted Amazon about sending it back within a couple of days of receiving it, but for some reason (maybe maturity?), I decided to keep it for another few days just to play with it a bit more.

I am so glad that I did. My only complaint is that I wish Amazon would have included some kind of cheat sheet to get users started. It would have gone a long way to prevent my initial meltdown. If my husband hadn't had his own Paperwhite for a month and shown me all of the basics, I can assure you that this model would be back in the hands of Amazon employees right now. They don't need to include some overwhelming instruction manual. Just one piece of paper with some simple "how to" notes would be perfect - I'd even be willing to draft something up for them!

Now that I've settled down with my Paperwhite, and have begun to take advantage of the outstanding benefits that it offers (i.e. instant dictionary, reading in the dark, lightweight and gorgeous, etc.) I would not part with it for anything. And my Keyboard is about to become a special gift to a friend who has always wanted a Kindle.
text_fidelity_b: Kindle Paperwhite 3G, 6" High Resolution Display with Built-in Light, Free 3G + Wi-Fi - Includes Special Offers [Previous Generation - 5th]

iParaAiluRy Soft Replacement Earpads Ear Pads Cushions for Logitech G35 G430 G930 F450 Headphones (1 Pair) My old G930 ear pads were flaking like crazy after several years of daily, all-day use, and I was hesitant to buy these at first because several people said they were too small. But I figured it's only $5, so it's worth a shot.

They arrived this morning and all I can think of is that whoever thought these were too tight or too small wasn't putting them on correctly. Maybe they thought they were just push-on instead of realizing that they have a flap (just like the ones that come with the headset) that needs to be lifted to go over the plastic part of the earpiece. That's what actually holds these things in place, people - otherwise they'd just fall off! Or maybe people aren't actually matching up the shape correctly. Either way - if you install them CORRECTLY, they fit perfectly.

These things are the correct size and I took some photos to compare the old Logitech-made pads with these. I also measured separately and they are the exact same size. If you take the time to look at how the original ear pads come off, you'll know exactly how to put these replacements on, and it'll take you all of about 10-15 seconds per ear pad.

These are virtually indistinguishable from the originals. I put these on and at first they seemed a little firmer than the original ear pads. However, I actually have a total of three G930 headsets (different purposes), so I was able to compare the feel of these ear pads to the original ear pads on one of the lesser-used, newer headsets. Again, pretty much identical - I guess they just get softer with use. Still, they are very comfortable even in their brand-new state, and I'm happy not to finish the day with black flakes on the sides of my face again.

I have three photos, two that are just comparing the back and front of the old pad to the replacement pad (and showing where the flap is that some people are apparently missing). The third photo is just showing the headset with one pad replaced so you can actually see that it looks pretty much the same as the original when installed correctly on the headset.

text_fidelity_a:
PDP Gaming Universal Media Remote – PlayStation 4, TV If you read the product description carefully, you won't waste time (as I did) trying to use this PLAYSTATION 4 UNIVERSAL MEDIA REMOTE to navigate PS4 games (e.g., Journey, Minecraft). The PS4 remote uses Bluetooth to turn your PS4 on and off, and to control and navigate PS4 media (e.g., DVDs), but only controls PS4 media. The PS4 remote can also be programmed to turn your TV, Cable Box, and Audio Receiver on and off, and to control and navigate those devices (assuming they accept remote Bluetooth operation).

The PS4 remote performs the advertised functions very well, and I'm happy with it. The main thing I wanted was the PS4 on/off feature, so that I wouldn't have to fool with the skinny button on the PS4 box when I wanted to play a DVD. But I also wanted something that would make it easier to navigate DVDs. I'm not much of a gamer, and I find the game controllers awkward to use. With the PS4 remote, the forward, back, play, and arrow buttons work "normally" (like any TV remote).

NOTE THAT once the PS4 remote is paired, you will turn the playstation "on" by pressing the big PS4 button, but you will turn it "off" by navigating to the PS4's power settings (in the display). (The PS4 remote doesn't have a "sources" button for bringing up the output options on my Samsung Smart TV, so I still need a second remote for selecting the PS4 output.)

The Bluetooth pairing and setup for the PS4 remote is straightforward, but you need to follow the directions in the accompanying booklet "to the letter". You have to visit several locations in the PS4 settings to add the remote to the PS4 device list, and then complete the setup.

Programming the remote to turn on another device (TV, Cable Box, Amplifier, etc.) is exactly the same as programming any universal remote. You turn on the device you're programming, put the remote into learning mode, point it at the device, and wait for the remote to find, recognize, and turn off the device. If the remote doesn't recognize the device, you must perform the device code programming manually (lots of codes are listed in the instruction booklet). The PS4 remote recognized my TV without difficulty, but my sound bar required manual programming.

Once you've programmed the various other devices, you switch between those devices by pressing the little labeled buttons (PS4, TV, AMP, CBL). Which brings me to the only thing that I don't like about the PS4 remote--the buttons (especially the switching buttons) are quite small, because there are so many of them packed onto this rather narrow remote.
text_fidelity_b: PDP Gaming Universal Media Remote – PlayStation 4, TV

text_fidelity_a:
Arteck 2.4G Wireless Keyboard and Mouse Combo Ultra Compact Slim Stainless Full Size Keyboard and Ergonomic Mouse for Computer/Desktop/PC/Laptop and Windows 10/8/7 Build in Rechargeable Battery ARTECK HW086MW162 Wireless Keyboard and Mouse combo, still charging that's why there are cables. Pen in the photo for size reference, along with the box it came in.

Unboxing was “frustration free” as advertised. I recycled my Logitech cord that connected to my desktop and inserted the USB receiver in it and it worked.

I plugged in the Micro USB charging cable to the keyboard and mouse. Only one Micro USB charging cable came with the combo so I used an extra Android Micro USB charging cable to charge both at the same time.

I was able to use the keyboard and mouse in a few moments. My computer automatically updated the files needed in a few minutes.

All in all the unboxing and set up was quick and effortless. Now I am going to explore the keyboard.

This keyboard has no number side keyboard that makes it smaller.

It has a blue function key to access page up, page down, home, and end, on the lower right where the left, right, up, down keys are.

Along the top with the F keys are blue function commands:

Escape has “Media” – when pressed opened Wave Pad, a NCH program I have installed.

F1 has an >/||, which did nothing when pressed

F2 has |<<, which did nothing when pressed

F3 has >>|, which did nothing when pressed

F4 has a speaker symbol )x, That mutes sound

F5 has a speaker symbol - which lowers volume

F6 has a speaker symbol + which increases volume

F7 has a symbol for home, which opens a new browser tab

F8 has a symbol of a magnifying glass that opens a search side window and uses Bing for search, when I clicked on one of the search results it opened a new Chrome tab. I had Chrome already opened.

F9 has a symbol for a folder, which did nothing when pressed

F10 has a symbol for power which turned off my computer. Since I had programs opened my computer asked for permission so I canceled.

F11 has “insert” on it which is pretty self explanatory

F 12 has “PrtSc” for print screen

The action on the keyboard is nice and a lot quieter than the Logitech keyboard I am replacing. The mouse action is good and also quiet.

For less than $23 this is a good keyboard and mouse. I never used the number keys on the side of my Logitech keyboard, which needed batteries, as did the mouse that came with it. The mouse had begun to do double clicks when I clicked once and the keyboard “enter” would stay down. That's why I replaced them for this Arteck Keyboard and Mouse combo. To be able to stop buying and replacing batteries and the small space it takes up, along with it is quiet, makes my money well spent.

The unit itself is really great. Ultimately I returned it because I was not working out for me. It's as simple as that.

The more complex nature of my unhappiness may come from the fact that I am a long-time Apple product user who really, really tried to go beyond the Apple brand. The Kindle Fire is a GREAT device - but when replacing an iPad it really didn't compare for me. Things sync'd seamlessly with my Apple products, but not the Kindle (I didn't expect it to, but I did miss that). I couldn't download some Apps that were unavailable for the Fire but available to other Droid interfaces. It took a bit of relearning how to navigate the Kindle, but that was fine (and very easy to do). The image was crisp, the response quick, the actual unit solid. It felt nice to hold in my hand, and the Origami case was a nice touch. But when push came to shove I ended up returning a perfectly good device because I just wasn't in love with it. I missed many of the features and uses that came naturally from my iPad. I may need to spend a bit more to get it, but if it is what truly works well for me without any sacrifice (other than about 200 dollars more)... then perhaps I should just save up and get the iPad.

It's embarrassing to admit all this, but it's true. I thought switching would be easy. The reviews are great - and the unit itself is truly great. But it just wasn't the right match for me and for my purposes. I'm heading back to the iPad.

MokerLink 8 Port PoE Switch with 6 PoE+ Port, 2 Uplink, 100Mbps, 78W AI Detection IEEE802.3af/at, Fanless Metal Plug & Play Network Switch This small, silent, unmanaged Ethernet switch has 8 super fast PoE ports (10/100Mbps) and 2 Gigabit Uplink ports (100/1000Mbps) that not only provide high speed internet but automatically detect if the plugged in device needs power and, if so, how much!

I did thorough testing on this unit over the last couple of months and I am thoroughly impressed by the performance.

By utilizing the built in chip this switch will provide up to 30 watts to every Ethernet device connected (up to a total of 120 watts) but will not provide any power to devices that do not require power. I found that this switch works absolutely flawlessly.

Having the capability to provide super fast internet speed and power at the same time makes this switch perfect for both business environments and as a hub for security systems.

I used this switch within my security system setup and mounted it within my attic to a beam with ease. I love that it is easily wall mountable but it can also be mounted within a rack with no problem.

I’ve tested my unit extensively using different security cameras and the results are nothing short of incredible. While most security cameras can be run via WiFi, nearly all of them still require a power adapter be plugged in. By utilizing this hub, security breaches are all but eliminated - by utilizing Ethernet instead of Wifi transmission your local storage unit makes it so there is no easy out of network access. In addition, transfer speed, resolution and picture quality is greatly increased - making the entire system more useful. In my experience, I found power is much easier to manage utilizing this method as opposed to having to run separate power supplies to each camera.

This is an all around outstanding product that I wouldn’t hesitate to recommend. This unit is sure to hold up well and perform even better.

text_fidelity_a:
Onkyo HT-S5100 7.1 Channel Home Entertainment System (Set of Nine, Black) (Discontinued by Manufacturer) The Onkyo HT-S5100 Home Entertainment System sounded quite good when listening to the radio, and I really loved the self-calibration feature to set the speaker phase/power-level based upon our optimum seating position.

When the receiver is played at low to mid volume ranges, the system was impressive, but there was distoration at higher levels when the speakers were driven beyond their capabilities.

As far as a Stereo Receiver goes, I'd give it high marks, but as far as a Home Entertainment system goes... in my opinion, I'd purchase something else.

I found after many frustrating hours of trying to get the receiver to work with my other HDMI components, that all of my attempts were in vain.

I'd essentially purchased the system on the recommedation of Consumer Reports (They crowed about the HT-S5100 having the best sound of any system they'd ever tested, and it was one of the only ones offering 7.1 versus 5.1 stereo surround).

I eventually re-read the Onkyo Owners Manual and found a small blurb regarding the audio of the system not working with HDMI...

I freely admit I'd blown-off the fact that analog/digital connectors were shown on the Quick Hook-Up illustrations (thinking these were alternative connections for those unlucky soul's who didn't have HDMI), when I finally resorted to contacting Onkyo for assistance/confirmation.

They confirmed my worst-fear, their HDMI's were (Pass-Though). When asked why they even bothered to put HDMI connectors on the system, the reply was (some consumers desired them).

Personally, I feel if a system has HDMI connectors present, that is implies they're fully compliant, otherwise their presence is misleading.

What this meant was all of my new toy's (50" Plasma, Blu-ray player, and Xbox 360) could only pass on video (not the higher quality audio signals through the HDMI connectors), and that I'd have to accept a lower quality audio output due to the use of standard audio connectors.

Perhaps I'd missed this in CR's review (or it wasn't stated), as I had to purchase additional digital cabling so that I could even hear the audio content of the devices hooked into the Onkyo (added expense/wiring woe's).

If I had to do it all over again, I'd purchase the HT-S5100 as a Stereo Receiver, but I wouldn't recommend it as the hub for a Home Entertainment System to interconnect your HDMI devices.

Another pearl-of-wisdom, don't rely strictly upon the written advice of a third-party, go out and listen/view the equipment yourself, as that's what I'm wishing I'd have done!
text_fidelity_b: Onkyo HT-S5100 7.1 Channel Home Entertainment System (Set of Nine, Black) (Discontinued by Manufacturer)

Geeni Sentry Wi-Fi Wireless Smart Floodlight Security Camera, 2-Way Audio, Motion Sensor Alarm, Audio Video Recording, Works with Alexa and Hey Google I have had the opportunity to review a few similar products over the last couple years and this new security light by Sentry has some great features that make it a stand out among other security lights.

I found installation straightforward and simple. For those who have trouble connecting to your WiFi, the most common issue is the strength of the different frequencies your router is broadcasting. The easiest way to resolve this is to go into your router settings via your computer and turn off the 5 GHz band during setup. This is necessary sometimes when initially setting up SmartHome products. While some may find this necessary for this product, I did not using my Orbi router system.

The Geeni App is easy to use and makes setup and customization of how the light operates user friendly.

This unit puts out a huge amount of light - 2100 Lumens to be exact while only using 24 watts of power thanks to it utilizing the LED bulbs.

This is the first security bulb I have reviewed that actually has a built in siren. This could be an outstanding feature if needed. Whether utilized to scare off someone attempting to break in to your home or to cause unwanted pests to run the other way - it will work! This siren is effective because it’s loud.

The speaker can also be used for communication purposes. By utilizing a built in microphone you’ll be able to have conversations with those you are viewing through the camera. The speaker and microphone have a surprisingly high clarity. The only thing I found odd with this aspect of this product is this is not a light you’ll want to place at head height as the light is so bright and the camera is really made to provide a wide angle view. Therefore when you speak through the speaker I found people usually look around and can’t figure out the source of the disembodied voice.

After using this product for the last 6 weeks I have found that it performs excellently. By installing a 128GB micro SD card within it, saving videos is easy and I’ve had plenty of time to review the footage. I love that it holds the recording locally so there is no cloud subscription fee required.

This is an excellent security light that will not only light the night when motion is detected, but will record it, alert you, scare the intruder with a siren or allow you to speak to them (or apologize for just scaring them with the siren).

This is an outstanding product that I definitely recommend.

2023 Amplified HD Digital TV Antenna Long 250+ Miles Range - Support 4K 8K 1080p Fire tv Stick and All TV's - Indoor Smart Switch Amplifier Signal Booster - 18ft HDTV Cable/AC Adapters Likes.

Well made.
Long cord. The long cord is very important.

Setup.

I used the long cord to place it on the floor, next to my patio door.
I then set my TV to auto scan.
It gave me many more stations than my non amplified leaf antennae pulled in.
Every station was crystal clear.
However, that was not a convenient permanent location, so I then placed it behind the TV.
It was important to first place it in the best possible area, in my case against the patio door to identify all possible stations.

Issues.

After auto scan identified all possible stations, I moved the antenna to behind my entertainment center. I lost half the stations. But, the TV showed those station numbers, it just couldn't pull them in. I then placed it flat on top of the entertainment center. It improved the reception. I then slid it partially inside my TV wall mount hardware, flat against the wall. It gave me excellent reception on all identified stations.

My advice.

Take advantage of the long cord, move it next to a window even if it won't be left there. You can then place the antenna in more convenient locations, trying to get back to as many identified stations as possible.
text_fidelity_b: 2023 Amplified HD Digital TV Antenna Long 250+ Miles Range - Support 4K 8K 1080p Fire tv Stick and All TV's - Indoor Smart Switch Amplifier Signal Booster - 18ft HDTV Cable/AC Adapters

text_fidelity_a:
Nuforce NE-700X Titanium Coated In-Ear Headphones - Aqua Silver Update after a couple of months

I still love 'em. Everything I put below still holds true. I rarely touch the EQ, and have been able to return to less processing is good processing listening.

One thing to add is that these are the first earbuds I could lay on my side with my head on the pillow and be comfortable. They have minimal strain relief but so far the cords have been perfect. I'd call tangle factor about medium.

++++++++++++++++++++++++++++++++++++++++++++++++++++++++++++++++++++++++++++
Original review

So far I've tried
Skull Candy Titan - For me the best bass sound in this bunch. Tight punchy, accentuated but enjoyably so. Good for working out. But I value accurate bass above all. So I just use these for working out now.
Vsonic GR99 - very nice balanced sounding for $20ish dollars
Vsonic VC02 - Great sounding, but not a lot of bass. But what bass that was there was VERY good. My favorite phones in this list. But I kept losing the ear piece because of the removable wires. After the 2nd time I moved onto the VSD1
Vsonic VSD1 - nice sounding, if somewhat dry. It didn't make me get into my music, and I couldn't get them comfortable in my ears
Brainwaves S1 - These were my least favorite, boomy and not very comfortable, heavy thick wires. The only pair of the above I returned.

What they do well - assume anything not here is more than adequate

Presentation - I feel like I'm getting what the engineer was going for in the mix. More musical than any of the above without falling into a 'warm sound'. A nice mix of forgiving and accurate. Brightness right about where it should be.
Sound Stage - Airy, instruments well placed. Center image is not the strongest, but not lacking. Does a nice job of presenting the room acoustics/reverb in the mix.
Drums - Drums are rendered very well, better than any of the the above.
Cymbals - rendered very well, especially high hat. You can tell the cymbals are made of metal, and not just the tik-tik of the drum stick tip
Treble-sibilance - Close to perfect. Nice and bright without getting into hissy/tizzy. Vocal articulation is good.
Very easy to listen to for long periods of time. They are accurate without being piercing or harsh.
Sounded good right out of the box.

Misc sound notes - distorted electric guitar is just right. They respond to EQ very well, (which the Brainwavz did not do). I really notice when something comes into the mix even if it is soft. And louder things like guitar solos, really punch in the way you hear when mixing in the studio.

If I HAD to critique the sound (this is a review) there is a very-very, (did I mention very?) lack of something in the mids. Think chest/throat area of male vocals. But this is in the realm of sound signature, a matter of taste, not a deficiency and in no way lowers my enjoyment of these.

Build - wires are thin and flexible which is what I wanted. Very nice for wearing over the ear. Microphonics close to none whether worn up or down. No hearing foot steps or wire rubbing/bouncing on clothes. Light cord/cinch is great for running.
Shape - Bullet shaped what can I say, they are light and comfortable. I like the ring of rubber around them. It gives a little grip for inserting/removing them.
I LOVE that they have a red strain relief on the right side. No having to get my glasses to see some tiny R or L printed somewhere. Cord is nice and long, which is nice for using on a treadmill or elliptical trainer, or for wearing the cord under your shirt or down in a pocket.

As much as I liked the over all presentation and frequency response I feel I should point out these are not hella flat-accurate phones (like the VC02). If a true hi-fi sound, bright/accurate/revealing, is what you are after I'd look elsewhere (maybe the VC02) Don't get me wrong, since I used to be a sound engineer, and work on electric guitars, and have very accurate/bright/revealing/fatiguing speakers on my desk, I'm very picky about good accurate sound. But that makes these musical, easy to listen to for very long periods of time and poorly recorded and/or lower quality rips won't be hard to listen to.

The title says it all - the best I've tried yet and the first phones that made me stop 'shopping' for my next pair of phones.

Listening setup. Listening has been through an amp and separate dac connected to my computer playing 192kb - 320k - FLAC music, and through my old Droid Charge (I use this because I can enable the onboard DAC) and my Samsung Note II listening to ripped music (192k or better) or Spotify/Pandora at their highest quality settings available in the premium versions.
text_fidelity_b: Nuforce NE-700X Titanium Coated In-Ear Headphones - Aqua Silver

text_fidelity_a:
Santana Samba by Carlos Santana, High Power Portable Bluetooth Speaker, 20W Outdoor Speaker, IP67 Dustproof & Waterproof Stereo Speakers, 20H Playtime, Powerful Extra Loud Volume with Rich Bass Our family is a bunch of speaker and ear phone fanatics. Everyone has different likes and I tend to like a well balanced music. Muffled really bugs me.

I wanted to have a nice balanced speaker that no one will take so I decided to get this one for ME. It has a nice solid housing and I figured it was worth getting since my favorite speaker seems to get misplaced a lot. Let's take a look.

WHAT IS THIS LIKE?
This is a very solid speaker. It is heavy duty and it has metal housing. The sides are not as fragile as others I have used which sound this good. It comes in a beautiful gift box which has cushioning and the typical Santana design to it. The speaker itself is pretty heavy so it is not something you toss in your backpack and run off with. It needs a bit more care than that.

CHARGING
This has a USB charger that will take about 4 hours to charge it up with. There is also a connection where you can get a FAST charger from the company, but you have to contact them for it. The charging cable comes with it just need a USB outlet. The directions warn to only use the original cable that comes with this to charge or there might be damage to the speaker. The voltage must be 5V with current rated at 115A.

CAN THIS RUN WHILE CHARGING?
I do not see in the instructions warnings against this, and it does work while plugged in.

PLAY TIME
This speaker runs out of juice pretty quickly. If you want it to last the entire time of 10 hours, I highly suggest you not put the volume up past 30%. Any higher and the battery time runs down pretty quickly. At 60% you are at the edge of running this down pretty quickly- as in 4 or 5 hours play time only.

PAIRING
I have had no issues pairing this with tablets or phones using Android. Just like when you turn the power on, it says PAIRING in a very loud voice so you will know when it is in pairing mode.

VOLUME
The volume button on this is tricky. If you are not thinking and just quickly press the volume once, instead of it getting slightly louder, you will skip a track. You have to press the volume down and not let up if you want the sound to go up or down depending on the button you press meaning +/-.

CARD SLOT
This speaker can also work off of a TF card (also known as a microSD card). You just have to change from bluetooth mode to card mode using the MODE button.

IS THERE AUX CAPABILITY?
I have an old MP3 player that has higher quality recordings than anything new I have. That only uses AUX and it works great with this.

PAUSE / PLAY
You can pause or play music with this using the MFB button

HOW DOES THIS PERFORM?
Let me tell you, this thing ROCKS. I mean it. This speaker is fabulous. Not only does it work great out of the box (after being fully charged) but it sounds better and better as you break it in. It fills the house with music that is great quality and does not have interference or any lag issues either.

WHAT ABOUT BASS, MIDS AND HIGHS?
I have to say that this speaker is one of the few that I have used which does a beautiful job of intense bass, balanced clear highs but the mids are not muffled at all. It is impressive and what I thought a speaker always should be.

CAN YOU USE TWO TOGETHER?
This allows you to add one other speaker to the system so you can have them in two places. I do not have another Europa speaker at the moment I can test that with.

THE BOTTOM LINE
Although this blows any other wireless speaker I have had out of the water, it does blow through power rather quickly unless the volume is pretty low. It is not only amazing out of the box (After charging) but it gets better with more use. This baby ROCKS.

MY RATING
Finding a speaker which does not overwhelm you with out of whack bass, piercing highs, or muffled middles is not always easy. This speaker seems to divide it all out very well. It is one of the nicest speakers I have used (wireless) to date. FIVE STARS!

Not only do I love this, but would definitely consider a second one along with the fast charger in the future to round out the whole system.

ANOTHER THING
This product has a notification on it that some of the proceeds from this product will go to help underprivileged children through the MILAGRO foundation (miracle) that Carlos Santana and his family started in 1998.
text_fidelity_b: Santana Samba by Carlos Santana, High Power Portable Bluetooth Speaker, 20W Outdoor Speaker, IP67 Dustproof & Waterproof Stereo Speakers, 20H Playtime, Powerful Extra Loud Volume with Rich Bass

ANTOP Omnidirectional HDTV Antenna Smartpass Amplified Outdoor 55/65 Miles Long Range AT-414B I've been collecting random TV antennas for review and from yard sales for years, and I think I've had about a dozen now. I generally only keep the two best ones. I tested this one out against my previous champion, which was just a single heavy duty rabbit ear on a magnetic base that somehow beat bigger, newer, and powered models.

The first thing I did with this when I got it was take it apart. I've gotten some in the past where the big plastic dish parts were just plastic for show and had nothing in them. Inside this one were multiple omnidirectional antennas and a circuit board. After attaching it to the coax, I checked through my channels and noticed I was missing some. I then added in the powered section, but didn't turn it on. This totally switched which channels I was missing. Then I turned it on and I got all my channels, plus another one I hadn't previously gotten, so it wins. The various parts do actually do something.

The pictures don't give much idea of scale. It's about the size of a steering wheel and comes with mounting plate. It's kind of huge and I wasn't pleased when I saw the size, but hey, I'll take the size if I get a brand new channel out of the deal.

I received a sample for review but the opinions are my own.
text_fidelity_b: ANTOP Omnidirectional HDTV Antenna Smartpass Amplified Outdoor 55/65 Miles Long Range AT-414B

text_fidelity_a:
Power Strip with 3 USB, KPSTEK Flat Plug Extension Cord with 2 Widely Spaced Outlets, Desktop Charging Station for Home, Office, Dorm Essentials, Black - KS2312 This is a combination product with a 5 foot extension cord, 2 AC power outlets, and 3 full-sized USB power ports. Compact size is great for travel, since older hotels don't have enough power outlets for modern travelers and the outlets are often hidden behind desks or under beds.

Unfortunately, the USB power ports are pretty weak. You get 2.4A divided among 3 ports, so if you're trying to charge 3 devices, each one gets less than 1A. Modern smartphones and tablets will often fast-charge at 3A, so charging with these ports will be very slow. USB powered laptops can use even more power and will complain about being charged at less than 3A.

I don't like that there is no USB-C charging port and no USB Power Delivery fast charging, which are becoming the standard for smartphones and laptops.

This device is not UL listed for electrical safety. As phone and tablet and laptop batteries get more and more powerful, electrical safety becomes more and more important. Most power strips from US brands are UL listed, so I cannot recommend a product that is not UL listed.
text_fidelity_b: Power Strip with 3 USB, KPSTEK Flat Plug Extension Cord with 2 Widely Spaced Outlets, Desktop Charging Station for Home, Office, Dorm Essentials, Black - KS2312

CyberPower CP685AVRLCD Intelligent LCD UPS System, 685VA/390W, 8 Outlets, AVR, Compact I have two of the larger Cyberpower UPS for my desktop systems and they have performed perfectly for the past (nearly) five years. So, when I needed a UPS for my cable modem and router I picked another Cyberpower. Since the draw on the two attached devices is so low I went with a lower capacity. They have other models that have about the same power output, but this model offers a screen to check load, run time, and other metrics while the unit is running. I've found that screen very helpful on my other UPS' so I went with this model.

Construction quality is very solid. There are 8 outlets - 4 for surge only (and are always on); 4 with surge and battery backup. The battery is replaceable, but I don't expect to have to do that anytime soon - both my other systems are running on their original batteries and still maintain a full charge after nearly 5 years of use.

My cable modem (a Motorola) and router (a Linksys) get about 60 minutes of run time off of the battery, which is more than enough for my needs.

I did not use the included software since I don't have a PC attached, so I can't comment on its features.

Highly recommend for a mid-level UPS system.
text_fidelity_b: CyberPower CP685AVRLCD Intelligent LCD UPS System, 685VA/390W, 8 Outlets, AVR, Compact

Netgear WGR614 Wireless-G Router We bought this Netgear WGR614 router back in March 2006. It installed somewhat easily and except for a little problem with the wireless PC card for the laptop (wouldn't be recognized at first but easily corrected) we had pretty stable use for about a year. Then we began to have connection problems. The connection would get slower and slower until internet pages would just not load, resulting in repeated "page cannot be displayed" errors. Powering down and restarting the router, modem and computer seemed to correct the issue. But as of this morning the router appears to have completely died. Powering down and restarting does nothing, the internet connection cannot be re-established. We can connect the desktop directly to the cable modem but for now the laptop is without connection, making for some unhappy family members here.

As of right now I don't know if we'll be buying another Netgear router & wireless PC card. The life expectancy of Netgear products does not appear to be all that great. Looking at some of the reviews we appear to be quite lucky that we got as much time out of the router as we did. Still I'm not in the mood to be shopping for a new router every 1.5 years or less. Hopefully there is a good router out there that can last at least two years.
text_fidelity_b: Netgear WGR614 Wireless-G Router

Have been using the Logitech Ultrathin Keyboard cover since 2012, when I received one as a gift. It changed my use of the iPad dramatically, it is now close to a laptop replacement much of the time. Now 3 years into it, it is wearing out. The iPad falls out backward, dangerously so, I have to be sure I don't leave it near the edge of a table lest it fall to the floor. I have always carried or packed the iPad with keyboard cover in an envelope case, and the only damage sustained was when it dropped out of the case to the floor. I do know someone who broke hers when it dropped off of the cover. Haven't put any skin covering on the iPad or case back, the iPad looks good the back of the keyboard a bit worn. The magnetic closure works well enough to position the closed case on the iPad, but I would not say it is strong enough to trust to stay closed.I can't see any magnet holding the iPad into the cover. Although I have been looking for other options, I probably will bite the bullet and get another one of these soon, as it seems to be the best combination of size, weight, usability and protection. Wouldn't consider going without a keyboard again.

Logitech M570 Wireless Trackball Mouse – Ergonomic Design with Sculpted Right-Hand Shape, Compatible with Apple Mac / Microsoft, USB Unifying Receiver, Dark Gray (Discontinued by Manufacturer) Update: 3/4/19

I've purchased a few of these. One did fail after a few years of intense use (I play Diablo 3 and a few MMOs, along with regular productivity/internet surfing.) Considering the price, and the amount of use these get, I have nothing but praise for these devices.

I will be honest: I reluctantly purchased this device. I've been using trackballs since around 1997 because my original computer space didn't really accommodate a standard mouse, and I really haven't gone back to mice. The corded Logitech Trackman has been my favored trackball for years. My cat chewed through the cord, and it eventually stopped working right, so I had to upgrade. Having a wireless trackball has always seemed rather redundant to me; why would you need cordless when you never move it? Well, it's actually quite nice to not fiddle with the cord! I didn't realize how annoying having a tether is until you no longer have it...

At any rate, this trackball is remarkably accurate (I play several games and work with large spread sheets,) and a snap to install. In short, a reluctant customer is very satisfied!
text_fidelity_b: Logitech M570 Wireless Trackball Mouse – Ergonomic Design with Sculpted Right-Hand Shape, Compatible with Apple Mac / Microsoft, USB Unifying Receiver, Dark Gray (Discontinued by Manufacturer)

Hyperion GPS Dash Cam with 4K Video Display and 120° Wide Angle View, Rechargeable with Built-in Mic, Lane Divergence and Collision Alerts The Hyperion auto dash camera is a decent dash cam for the money. It is easy to install and the suction cup holder is very secure. You can choose three different video resolutions; 1296P, 1080P, or 720P. The higher the resolution the shorter the recording duration before the video starts loop recording. You can increase memory by inserting a higher capacity memory card, it comes with a 16GB memory card installed already and it can take a 32GB or up to a 64GB memory card. The recording modes/video files are, Crash detected, Loop-recording, Parking and Photo. You can plug your camera to you computer with the supplied cable to transfer the videos or you can pop out the memory card and put it in a card reader on your computer to transfer the videos. You can also update the camera the same way, if there is an update to the camera.

The camera has other functions as well, it has Advanced Driver Assistance Systems (ADAS), Lane Departure Warning System (LDWS), Front Collision Warning System, Front Vehicle Departure Warning. They seem to work, but I wouldn't rely on it. It just give beeping tones and sometimes it seems random whey they go off, also if you pass other drivers or vice versa it beeps as well. The good thing is in the menu settings, you can disable the alarms and it doesn't affect the camera recording.

Installation is pretty simple, it comes with a long power cord that can be easily concealed under the trim. The only thing that might be a problem is you need to plug it into the cigarette lighter, so if you don't have another lighter plug outlet, you would have to unplug the camera to for example plug in a cellphone charger. The camera does have a rechargeable battery built in so it can run on battery power for a while, but you have to have the camera plugged in for a while to charge the battery first.

Overall, this is a nice camera and I am very happy with it.
text_fidelity_b: Hyperion GPS Dash Cam with 4K Video Display and 120° Wide Angle View, Rechargeable with Built-in Mic, Lane Divergence and Collision Alerts

NETGEAR Orbi Compact Wall-Plug Whole Home Mesh WiFi System - WiFi router and wall-plug satellite extender with speeds up to 2.2 Gbps over 3,500 sq. feet, AC2200 (RBK20W) This is an updated version of a mesh system router and satellite I already have. The technology is great when it's working, but, for whatever reason, my system has needed to be reset once a week or more, and the coverage is nowhere near as good as it claims it should be.

My hope was that the newer version would be faster and have better coverage. It isn't. It doesn't. And, like the earlier version, it has to be in AP mode to work with my FIOS modem (FIOS has a version of this available with its own firmware, but you have to buy a new one, and it won't work with any other ISP). Those hopes dashed, my next hope was that I could at least use the router as a satellite on my existing system, which, of course not.

So, you would think I could at LEAST use the satellite from the new one with the old system or the old satellite with the new one? They are the same model, after all. And that, too, would be a nope.

What I finally did, after hours on the internet (and other hours just trying to set up the new one by itself - it was the same with the old one - it for some reason despises custom settings and will not save them the first many times. It will also lose them after firmware upgrades, I expect, like its predecessor), was set it up alongside the old one with its own network name. Now I have one network serving one side of the house and the other serving the other. Speeds are good. So far, no routing issues, and I don't really expect any. The two network solution seems to have worked well for others.

But really.

If you are looking to expand your Orbi network, check out the nighthawk mesh expanders. I have the 7500, and it's excellent. Also, don't take my lukewarm review for a no-rec. The Orbi is, as far as I can tell from personal experience, buggy and locked down, but, again from personal experience, it beats the Velop (its nearest competitor) by a mile for coverage.
text_fidelity_b: NETGEAR Orbi Compact Wall-Plug Whole Home Mesh WiFi System - WiFi router and wall-plug satellite extender with speeds up to 2.2 Gbps over 3,500 sq. feet, AC2200 (RBK20W)

I’ve spent right at a week with them and this is what I’ve found.

There are little to no instructions regarding these headphones and I had to research the app that has to be downloaded and go to the Razer website to begin using. Once I had everything set up, it was easy. I would have rather had a semblance of instruction than the wild packaging. The headphones were easy to pair to my phone and the sound is crystal clear. I was impressed with the noise cancelation especially. As an audiophile, I am very, very critical of sound and what is missing with these headphones is any kind of upper volume range or bass. For the price, I would have expected better in that department.

The strongest plus to these headphones is the clarity of the music. Even with the lower volume and the lack of bass, the music is sharp and clear - something I have found gets lost with other brands. The noise cancellation is also a strength above others.

Overall, I would recommend if you’re not searching for heavily bassed or volumed headphones.

text_fidelity_a:
GL.iNet GL-E750 (MUDI) 4G LTE OpenWrt VPN Router, T-Mobile ONLY,128GB Max MicroSD, 7000mAh Battery, OpenVPN, WireGuard, Tor, a Router That You can Program (EP06-A), for North America only I love GL.iNet. They create routers based on OpenWRT, which has so many great features that you'd find in professional level routers that cost thousands of dollars. There is a fairly steep learning curve to it, though. Fortunately, GL.iNet understands this and makes things easier by creating their own customizations to the firmware to make OpenWRT easier to use and more custom to the routers themselves.

The GL.iNet GL-E750 (MUDI) is their latest 4G LTE router. Pop in a sim card and the router will create a hotspot that routes to the LTE network. For additional protection, it is easy to set up the router to connect to a VPN provider. By connecting the router to VPN, all client computers connecting to it WIFI will be protected.

I used this router during my last trip and it was GREAT. I have a few devices that I bring with me. A laptop, tablet, and phone. I even bring a firetv with me sometimes. While in the car, I have the router connecting everyone's devices to the Internet via LTE and when I got to the hotel, I connected the router to the hotel's wifi and turned on VPN. The transition from LTE to hotel wifi was seamless. Not only did I not need to reconfigure everyone's devices to connect to the hotel WIFI, we were also secure behind the router's firewall and VPN connection.

The two restrictions that this product may present to potential buyers is first, the price. It is quite pricey and it can be hard to justify its purchase. Especially when you can get a travel router for around $40 with the ability to tether a phone via USB. The second issue is that this specific router is tied down to the T-Mobile network with no ability to unlock it for other networks (according to the seller's response in the questions section of for this product). If the convenience and the ability to fully control the TTL to bypass t-mobile's tethering throttling restrictions is important to you, it may justify the price you'd be paying.
text_fidelity_b: GL.iNet GL-E750 (MUDI) 4G LTE OpenWrt VPN Router, T-Mobile ONLY,128GB Max MicroSD, 7000mAh Battery, OpenVPN, WireGuard, Tor, a Router That You can Program (EP06-A), for North America only

Mediasonic ProBox HF2-SU3S2 4 Bay 3.5” SATA HDD Enclosure – USB 3.0 & eSATA Support SATA 3 6.0Gbps HDD transfer speed I have had this unit for about four years now. Never a problem. I use it for storing media files and my digital Paintings. It was used for four years on a MacPro 3,1, connected via USB 2. Upgraded the drives over the years, so now it has two 4TB and two 2TB Seagate HDDs.
I just purchased a new (to me) MacPro Trash Can, so I will try the USB 3.
This enclosure is heavy, and not bad looking. The plastic faceplate comes off easy (as it was probably designed to do, to allow easy changing the Hard Drives). But again chances are once you get the drives installed and settings just so, you will not be messing with the door/faceplate. it has tow plastic pins on the bottom and a "latch (Spring loaded)" press and it pops off or on.
The power cord goes in the side, which is weird but not a deal breaker. And unusual configuration, but it is pretty solid and really I don't really mess with it very oftern).
Three fan settings and yes two of them are not quiet. I leave mine on auto and unless I am working on a hot day, moving or writing tons of files, don't hear the fan at all).
The LED lights are not an issue for me, but I could see where in a dark room it would bother some folks. (electrical tape if it really errkks you).
Getting the settings the way you want them takes some trial and error, but once you have them you will most likely not mess with them again.
Drives are easy to add or remove, a couple screws, slide it in the slot.
I have found that if the drive has been formatted and contains data when you add it, you have to force mount it, but once that is done no issues.
So if possible initialize the drive in the enclosure.
This is ideal for novice of mid-level tech geeks, or folks who have a large media collection (Music, movies, photos, etc).
I have hooked it up directly to my Mac Pro and my Wireless router (Orbi) so anyone authorized to access the network can access the media files on it. So my Photos on one drive, Movies on two drives and music on the last drive.
I would highly recommend this to anyone wanting to create a media server.
It DOES NOT have RAID built-in, it can be added via software, but, for a few bucks more you can get the RAID version of this.
text_fidelity_b: Mediasonic ProBox HF2-SU3S2 4 Bay 3.5” SATA HDD Enclosure – USB 3.0 & eSATA Support SATA 3 6.0Gbps HDD transfer speed

text_fidelity_a:
Asus Transformer Pad Infinity TF700T-B1-GR 10.1-Inch 32GB Tablet (Amethyst Gray) I debated for a long time about getting a tablet. A couple years ago I'd have sworn that I'd never have one. I've been a laptop guy for a long time and love the PC, but it gets cumbersome some times. You can't do everything with a tablet that you can with a PC, but for most people it can fill most of your needs. Smart phones are nice but they're just to small for my eyes and big fingers. Besides, my view of cell phones is something to make calls with and talk on.

That said as I read and looked at different tablets, I realized the potential for their use. I've got issues with Apple and didn't want to go the ipad route for a number of reasons. I did some research on the new Windows tablets and I like the idea, but they've got a way to go. I think they rushed it to get it to market. I like the ideas behind Android and although a lot of the apps are designed more for smart phones, apps optimized for tablets are increasing and all the other smart phone designed apps work. The open source design makes for all sorts of obscure market apps. Plenty of developers out there. You can find some weird stuff for Android that you won't find on other platforms. Lots of pretty good free apps and plenty of cheap stuff too that is impressive.

So next I had to decide on size. For 99% of my uses, the 10 inch seemed to be the better choice and with a number of these with docking key pads available, I went that way rather than the smaller versions. So then I had to decide which one. It didn't take long to realize that ASUS was probably the leader in the field and known for very high quality products. Likewise it only took a bit longer to see that the Infinity TF700 with 64GB, was the machine to have. I also opted for the docking keypad.

The tablet is very impressive. The screen resolution is right up there with the best ipad. The NVIDIA quad core CPU is a screamer. Can't get much better. Cameras are very good. Battery life is good and amazing with the dock which also has a battery in it. With all the features together, I think this is the best Android tablet out there today and most pro revues agree.

As a new user to this scene, I'm sure others may have different ideas that got me to this choice, but I can say that I am completely satisfied. That said, as a "newbie" I suppose you might think anything would seem that way, however, I did a lot of research and hands on comparisons and I'm comfortable I bought the best.

I am 99.9% thrilled with it. If it has a flaw, it's probably the speaker which faces the wrong way in my opinion and doesn't have quite the volume and sound quality I'd like. It is fine in a quiet environment, but if there's any background noise it leaves a bit to be desired. I have found that if you hold it with your hand somewhat loosely cupped behind the speaker, the sound level improves dramatically as your hand reflects if towrd you. It is fine with ear buds and I also recently picked up a great little bluetooth speaker, (Clalrity HD by Monster), that kicks butt.

Everything else about the Infinity TF700 seems perfect. The only other way to make it better would be built in 4G and phone capability. If I'm mobile I use mine with a Verizon Jet Pack, which is an awesome device itself. Even on 3G it works better than my built in mobile broadband in my laptop.

Do your own research and get some hands on time if you can to compare because all tablets are not equal. There is no doubt that as far as tablets go, a lot has to do with how you will use it and what for. But if you want the best Android tablet in the 10 inch size range, you can't beat the Infinity TF700. This thing is awesome!
text_fidelity_b: Asus Transformer Pad Infinity TF700T-B1-GR 10.1-Inch 32GB Tablet (Amethyst Gray)

NETGEAR Orbi Pro WiFi 6 Tri-Band Mesh System (SXK50), Router with 1 Satellite Extender for Business or Home, VLAN, QoS, Coverage up to 5,000 sq. ft, 75 Devices, AX5400 802.11 AX (up to 5.4Gbps) The rise of home automation devices means that many of us have a lot more devices that connect to our wifi networks. While most of those devices use the 2.4Ghz frequency while devices like phones, tablets, and firetv use 5Ghz to stay out of each other's way, it still means that there are so many more devices to manage in a network and all of them are attempting to talk on the network. Not to mention interference from neighbors and their many devices.

This drives the need for beefy routers with faster CPUs to manage all of the chatter and radios that allow many more simultaneously connected devices.

The NETGEAR Orbi Pro WiFi 6 Tri-band Mesh System (SXK80) attempts to address these needs. Sporting the latest wireless Wifi 6 technology, most of the basic features that a router needs (QoS, DDNS, VPN), and 60+ device support, the SKX80 holds a lot of promise.

Unlike one of the upvoted reviews, I don't have a different AX system to compare this to so for me, this mesh router performs admirably. It is fast and has good coverage. In my time so far, I haven't had any dropped connections. Videos stream well and web browsing works fine. I don't normally do voice or video calls while walking around the house, but watching videos while walking seem to work well. My device will jump from router to satellite correctly and there is no disruption to the video playback.
text_fidelity_b: NETGEAR Orbi Pro WiFi 6 Tri-Band Mesh System (SXK50), Router with 1 Satellite Extender for Business or Home, VLAN, QoS, Coverage up to 5,000 sq. ft, 75 Devices, AX5400 802.11 AX (up to 5.4Gbps)

Samsung Galaxy Tab 2 (10.1-Inch, Wi-Fi) 2012 Model I thought long and hard about a tablet, knowing that for me it would basically be a toy. Plus I already had a Nook Color. When the iPad2 reduced in price, I thought about getting one of those, but decided against it for the following reasons: (1) no Flash--and yes, I know HTML5 is going to make that obsolete, but in the meantime many websites have a lot of money invested in Flash animation and even restaurants use the silly format to show you their menus (geez, just give us a LIST already--I don't need pretty pictures to find out if you serve something I can eat) and (2) I'm already invested in the Android market and would have to buy many iPad apps that I already have free from Android.

I have not even used it for a week yet, but this a preliminary review with some information I saw requested in other reviews (not necessarily here at Amazon).

UPS delivered this a little before 6:30 p.m. I immediately plugged it into the charger and left it alone. It was charged by 10 p.m. (it might have been earlier, but the unit was away from me and I heard no bleep or flash that might have have indicated the charge was finished). So it does not take six or eight or ten hours to charge as I have seen claimed on other sites. By midnight I was attached to wireless, had gotten into all my accounts and Android apps and was happily surfing and rearranging my home screen.

I used this over the weekend at a science fiction convention. I did not use it constantly, but turned the screen on and off all day for about a 12-hour period, reading Facebook and blogs, checking the news and weather, looking at the convention schedule online, playing short You Tube videos, etc. Nothing excessive, but sometimes did have it on for a half hour to 45-minutes at the time. I also do not have a lot of widgets going, like the Accu-Weather and news widgets that come pre-loaded on the home screen. (They delete easily.) In that 12-hour period it never got below 78% on the battery. It's very quick and fast and responds to a Targus stylus (rubber tipped) wonderfully, much better than my Nook color. The resolution of the screen is impressive. Maybe it's not the new iPad's "retinal display," but it's very, very sharp and bright, even though I keep my brightness turned down to save power. I downloaded the Nook app and the magazines I subscribe to look gorgeous and are simple to read; if not, a tap of the screen makes the text bigger. The unit also comes with Zinio preloaded, an app I plan to use to subscribe to non-US magazines. Kindle books look nice as well, but to me this is too large for marathon reading sessions. I prefer my Nook Color for that. Like my Android phone and my Nook Color, it connects to wireless like a dream, which is more than I can say for my laptop.

Things that might lead you to choose another tablet: (1) The camera is nothing special. It takes good close ups, but further away was problematic. However, I was in a low-light situation each time. Taking photos outside may be totally different. Why Samsung chose to remove the flash I have no idea. Silly, really. But who buys a tablet to take pictures with? (2) With a stylus I can tap to enlarge an image (like Google Maps), but not make it smaller and there is no plus or minus sign on the screen as on my Android phone. (3) Blogger doesn't work in the browser; you have to download the Blogger app, but that works well. iExit doesn't work on it, either. Rats. (4) As at least one other person mentioned, the screen cap button is right in a place where you can hit it easily. I thought of a good use for it this weekend (took a screen cap of the online schedule for the convention I was at, made a short-cut of it to the screen, then pulled up the screen cap for reference rather than going to the web page all the time). Very convenient! (5) Hate the pre-loaded websites in the browser, but I have seen this on other tablets. Apparently we the public are stupid (or lazy) and can't find our own favorite websites and bookmark them. [eyes roll], and (6) my Bluetooth keyboard won't work with it right now because there is as yet no driver for Android 4.0 (Ice Cream Sandwich).

I hope to check back with further comments.

[A few weeks later after I bought this, my husband found an Asus Transformer (TF300) at a good price. It appears to be just as good as this Samsung and the camera is better. It has a zoom and does take a better photo. So if you were looking for a tablet with a better camera the Asus Transformer may be for you. Note: It doesn't have a flash either.]

[Update July 31, 2012 to answer "How long does the battery last"?: I was sick and tired of not seeing any Olympic equestrian coverage except for a couple of hours in the wee hours of the morning, so downloaded the "Live Extra" Olympics app from the Android Market. This carries live streaming of events as well as archived events. This morning I watched about two hours of live streaming of the jumping finals. When that ended I watched six hours of cross-country eventing replay. Then about an hour and forty minutes of the replay of the jumping. I had my brightness at about 35%. This got me down to 10% of the battery from a full charge. Quite satisfactory.]
text_fidelity_b: Samsung Galaxy Tab 2 (10.1-Inch, Wi-Fi) 2012 Model

text_fidelity_a:
SleepPhones AcousticSheep Classic | Corded Headphones for Sleep, Travel, and More | The Original and Most Comfortable Headphones for Sleeping | Soft Gray - Fleece Fabric (Size M) I fall asleep to audiobooks, and have tried a lot of speakers and headphones with mixed results. My husband bought me these AcousticSheep SleepPhones recently, and what a difference they make! They're very comfortable - okay, the mediums are a little large for me, but I've found a way to position them so they work perfectly. The speakers are thin and pliable, so they're comfortable even if you roll over and lie on them, and the sound is pleasant - not too boomy or too shrill, and you can move the headband so you can listen in both ears or only one, if you prefer.

The one catch is that the wires leading out of the headphones are pretty thin, and judging my previous experience using many headsets and speakers in bed, they're going to break inside at some point. Then I'll either have to order more or perhaps do a little creative wire work and attach new, stronger wires. I'd be perfectly happy to replace these once a year as they've improved my quality of sleep (I'm used to waking when I roll onto a hard plastic speaker or earphone).

BTW, the headband itself is sooo soft and comfy - none of the headbands I've used on my hair over the years are this cozy.

Like it said on the package, these truly are pajamas for your ears ;-)

***Update Feb 9, 2014***

It's been just short of a year since I write the above review. Since then, I ordered a second smaller pair of SleepPhones, the band of which wasn't as soft and furry, but it was good for wearing when doing housework. This one didn't come in the same packaging - the packaging was more minimual. My original pair of SleepPhones' wire on the left ear did indeed break, and I bought a third pair. This was in a much smaller package, but was furry and comfy as the first set. Hopefully it will last a bit longer than my original pair - the wires are a bit more robust.
text_fidelity_b: SleepPhones AcousticSheep Classic | Corded Headphones for Sleep, Travel, and More | The Original and Most Comfortable Headphones for Sleeping | Soft Gray - Fleece Fabric (Size M)
